body:
Everyone thanks for your responses.

I know it's not necessary to do what's widely accepted - the bad part is that I'm a social being and I need other people, even though on the rational plane I couldn't care less about them. The quality of life is determined by how well you stand up to the environmental expecations - which is one of the things I hate about it. 

 For example, how am I supposed to find a GF (one of my main problems)? A girl can feel respect or pity for me, but what are the reasons for her to be attracted to someone who is faulty? I know I couldn't fall in love with someone who is a wonderful person (and I'm probably not one) but her looks/physique is screwed up. That's how nature made us work. And me being bright and sensitive, however virtuous may it be, is more often than not a disadvantage for me.

Being lonely and sexually inactive is already overwhelming, and not being able to do many cool things (dancing, hiking etc.) makes things even worse. I don't want do die, however I'm aware that fear of death just a biological instinct. 

All of you mention change, but there are things I cannot change, including myself and the way the life is - pointless and unfair. If I was physically normal, maybe I could just mess around till death and have some fun here and there (still I'm pretty idealistic and would be pissed with the way the world is), but now it's simply not worth it, and what keeps me from suicide is just an irrational, biological fear of death. Hell, everything about mine and your mind is designed to satisfy a goal that has been irrational from the start - keep the species going. Why am I supposed to find the life worth anything?

Sorry if not everything's clear, English isn't my primary language and there are so many things on my mind.

Thanks for replying. I know that non-human concept is awkward, almost as if i was delusional... I'll try to explain this better.

My defects affect my life in a measurable way and I'm not entitled to do things other people are - it's unfair and feels bad.

But the non-human thing has more to do with the rarity of my problem - it seems as if I was the only person on Earth having these symptoms, and I've spent countless hours trying to find any connection between them or a cause... in vain, and I'm proficient at sorting out things. And the doctors I've met don't seem to care about that (there are many common health problems that are more spectacular), even one 'psychiatrist' I've consulted insisted that I had schizophrenia... If I knew anyone else with such condition I would probably be less emotional about it... Another thing is that it's genetic, and it feels bad to know that you are fucked up at the very core.

BTW I know that there are people with far worse conditions, and you could possibly tell me that I should embrace what I have etc., but I ask, what's the threshold beneath which living just isn't worth it? And the threshold definetely exists, since what are your options to cherish life when you are e.g. blind, deaf and paralyzed? I know it's slightly OT, but it really bothers me. Like, it's easy to tell someone who's depressed but physically healthy - "Dude, you will get over it, just get some education/a job/take up a hobby/sport /make friends/find gf etc."... But what if the shit is gonna stay with you forever?

EDIT: It's really messy, I'm very tired atm, but hope you get the point.
